plan: Since this ascending clock auction with sealed exit bids functions like a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid/clock price when others exit), truthful bidding is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value of $23 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids and pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the winner pays the highest losing bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable to do so (when my value exceeds others' bids) and never pay more than my value if I win. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid $18, my true value.

This mechanism functions like a second-price auction: my sealed bid sets my exit point, and I win only if I have the highest bid, paying the second-highest bid. Bidding exactly my true value ($39) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit since I only pay less than my value if I win, and bidding higher or lower than value only reduces expected profit without changing the price I'd pay when winning.
